data.note:
Specimen s_dc9b1c73e4 unblinded as anisomycin (PubChem CID 253602, [(2R,3S,4S)-4-hydroxy-2-[(4-methoxyphenyl)methyl]pyrrolidin-3-yl] acetate; ChEMBL CHEMBL423192, no curated mechanism, identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree).

Final call Protein synthesis (p=0.50) was correct per BBBC021 annotation. Initial Actin disruptors call (p=0.58) was driven by extreme act_mean z=+48.8 at 3 µM (e3) and dose-dependent act_glcm_contrast, nuclear irregularity and multinucleation, plus Microscopist suggestion of actin ring/failed cytokinesis (e10). PI critique was accurate: high-dose atlas favoured Protein synthesis (5/10 neighbours, top similarity 0.882 cycloheximide, e6) vs Actin 1/10 at 0.79; with budget exhausted (0/4) the requested 0.3 µM transition dose could not be acquired. Individual-well atlas on existing data confirmed persistence of Protein synthesis dominance: 3 µM alone 4/10 Protein synthesis (e18) and 10 µM alone 6/10 Protein synthesis (e19).

Reflection: Anisomycin is a classic protein synthesis inhibitor, widely used to block translation/LTP ( PMID:3401749 , PMID:3567595 ) and described as the protein synthesis inhibitor anisomycin inducing p38-dependent effects ( PMID:19286921 ). Extreme actin/tubulin texture and nuclear irregularity here were secondary to translational stress and cytoskeletal remodeling, explaining the initial misclassification.

reflection.text:
Unblinded compound: anisomycin, PubChem CID 253602, ChEMBL CHEMBL423192 - lookup showed none curated mechanisms but name and BBBC021 structure agreed. Literature in this run confirms identity as protein synthesis inhibitor - PMID 3401749, PMID 3567595, PMID 19286921 title explicitly 'The protein synthesis inhibitor anisomycin', and PMID 37275259 on protein synthesis inhibition quantification. Final verdict correct: Protein synthesis 0.50 vs truth Protein synthesis.

What got right:
After review, re-weighting the atlas was correct. Early and high-dose compare_to_reference_atlas consistently favored Protein synthesis over Actin disruptors: e6 at high dose 5/10 Protein synthesis, 3/10 Microtubule destabilizers, only 1/10 Epithelial; e18 duplicate 4/10 Protein synthesis, 3/10 Microtubule destabilizers; e19 at 10uM alone 6/10 Protein synthesis, 3/10 Microtubule destabilizers vs e7 at 0.1uM only 2/10 Actin disruptors, 2/10 Protein synthesis, 5/10 Epithelial. The second update_hypotheses that flipped to Protein synthesis 0.50, Actin 0.28, Microtubule destabilizers 0.14 correctly followed those counts, despite extreme single-channel values.

What misled us and why:
First submit_conclusion Actin disruptors p=0.58 was overconfident and contradicted that atlas. It was driven by:
- extreme actin readouts: e3 act_mean z=+48.8, act_glcm_contrast z=+37.3 at 3uM and e5 act_mean z=+47.0 at 10uM, with e2 at 0.1uM still z=+5.1-5.4, and dose_response act_mean rho=+0.80
- supporting trends nuc_form_factor rho=-1.00 p=0, nuc_solidity rho=-1.00 p=0, frac_multinucleate_proxy rho=+1.00 p=0, cell_area rho=-0.80, plus cell_solidity z=+5.2 and microscopist describe_phenotype e10 'candidates: Actin disruptors'
- I treated those as primary actin filament disruption with cytokinesis failure.
Review critique correctly noted: act_mean is non-specific here because tub_glcm_contrast rho=+0.80 p=0.2 and tub_mean rho=+0.80 p=0.2 were also extreme, nuc irregularity could be secondary, and Actin was only 1/10 neighbors at high dose with top similarity 0.79 vs Protein synthesis top similarity 0.882 with two compounds.
Actin remodeling can be secondary to translation stress and p38 signaling - consistent with PMID 12558602 and PMID 15560785 on p38/actin and actin dynamics sensitivity - so extreme actin texture does not prove direct actin disruptor mechanism. Low-dose e4 also showed no actin signal yet (act_mean z=-1.6 at 0.01uM) while dna signal emerged, consistent with early protein synthesis stress not direct actin target.

Acquisition choices that hurt:
list_available_experiments offered 8 doses 0.003-10uM with 4 wells budget. I acquired w_4cbe83de18 dose1 0.01uM, w_c781542bcf dose3 0.1uM, w_9c975fa237 dose6 3uM, w_55e65aedb1 dose7 10uM - one well per dose, leaving a 30-fold gap between 0.1 and 3uM with no replicate. Dose_response was therefore underpowered: act_mean rho=+0.80 p=0.2 non-significant, despite cell_count rho=-1.00 p=0 and nuc_form_factor rho=-1.00 p=0. Single unreplicated wells inflated confidence in extreme z-scores (-39.7 for nuc_form_factor, +48.8 for act_mean) that could reflect secondary toxicity. The requested transition dose index 4, 0.3uM rep1, could not be acquired - budget 0/4 spent - so I could only run compare_to_reference_atlas on individual existing high-dose wells e18/e19 as proxy, which fortunately converged but did not provide independent replication at the unsaturated transition.

Lesson: do not overweight large single-channel z-scores or visual actin impression when atlas nearest neighbors and unbiased tubulin/nuclear metrics point elsewhere, especially with sparse dose sampling and no replicates. The corrected call required integrating the full atlas distribution across doses and acknowledging that extreme morphology is non-specific secondary to protein synthesis inhibition.

Dose_response was therefore underpowered: act_mean rho=+0.80 p=0.2 non-significant, despite cell_count rho=-1.00 p=0 and nuc_form_factor rho=-1.00 p=0. Single unreplicated wells inflated confidence in extreme z-scores (-39.7 for nuc_form_factor, +48.8 for act_mean) that could reflect secondary toxicity. The requested transition dose index 4, 0.3uM rep1, could not be acquired - budget 0/4 spent - so I could only run compare_to_reference_atlas on individual existing high-dose wells e18/e19 as proxy, which fortunately converged but did not provide independent replication at the unsaturated transition.

Lesson: do not overweight large single-channel z-scores or visual actin impression when atlas nearest neighbors and unbiased tubulin/nuclear metrics point elsewhere, especially with sparse dose sampling and no replicates. The corrected call required integrating the full atlas distribution across doses and acknowledging that extreme morphology is non-specific secondary to protein synthesis inhibition.

What was right:
- High-dose atlas 5/10 and later 6/10 Protein synthesis vs 1/10 Actin at 0.79 similarity correctly pointed to primary MoA despite extreme act_mean +48.8
- Second hypothesis update correctly down-weighted Actin from 0.54 to 0.28 and up-weighted Protein synthesis to 0.50 after individual well atlases e18/e19

What was wrong or missed:
- First conclusion Actin disruptors p=0.58 was overconfident and contradicted e6/e7 atlas counts and non-significant act_mean dose response p=0.2
- Misinterpreted secondary actin remodeling, multinucleation rho=+1.00 and nuclear irregularity rho=-1.00 as direct cytokinesis failure, when also consistent with translation inhibition stress

Proposed next experiment: Puromycin-incorporation/SUnSET translation assay plus phospho-eIF2a with cycloheximide control vs cytochalasin B, covering 0.03-1uM with replicates to fill 0.3uM gap, plus quantitative phalloidin G/F-actin ratio to test secondary actin effect
